answer: Subsurface seismic attestation counters Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to ambient vibration profiles measured in basalt bedrock beneath a marine wharf. Agents sample local tremors, binding telemetry under an asymmetric cipher to prove co-location with dedicated geophones. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware expense of deploying separate physical seismometers per node. However, heavy tidal surge induces acoustic drift that can falsely reject legitimate agents.
